# signing/testdata — Interop Fixtures

This directory contains fixture files used by `interop_test.go` to verify that
our Minisign implementation produces and parses the correct wire format.

## Fixture files

- `upstream_payload.bin` — the raw payload that was signed
- `upstream.pub` — the Minisign public key that signed it
- `upstream.minisig` — the resulting .minisig file

## Fixture source

These fixtures were **generated by our own implementation** (not by the upstream
`minisign` binary). This is an acknowledged limitation: without the upstream
binary available in the build environment we cannot generate true upstream
fixtures. The format-shape test (`TestOurSignatureVerifiesAsUpstreamLayout`)
validates that our output is structurally identical to what upstream would
produce. The integration test (`TestUpstreamCLIVerifiesOurSignature`, behind
`//go:build integration`) closes the us→upstream interop gap when the upstream
binary is available.

## Regenerating with upstream `minisign` (minisign >= 0.9)

To replace these fixtures with real upstream-generated artifacts:

```bash
# Generate a keypair (passphrase: empty — press Enter twice)
minisign -G -p upstream.pub -s upstream.key

# Sign the payload
minisign -S -s upstream.key -m upstream_payload.bin -t "timestamp:1234567890"

# The .minisig file is written to upstream_payload.bin.minisig
# Rename it:
mv upstream_payload.bin.minisig upstream.minisig
```

For Argon2id-encrypted keys (private key KDF = Ar), upstream `minisign >= 0.11`
is required (released 2023). Scrypt-encrypted keys (KDF = Sc) work with any
version.

## AC#7 interop verification

The in-process format-shape test runs unconditionally with `go test ./signing/...`.

The full upstream-CLI verification (us → upstream) requires the upstream
`minisign` binary on PATH:

```bash
go test -tags integration ./plugin-sdk/signing/...
```
